egress.terms: direct WireGuard where possible; the cloud relay otherwise, at an unpublished rate

chaining: signalling with a relay fallback; self-hosting removes the machine cap and adds a server to run.

limits.value: no number: the cloud-hosted Reverse Proxy is 'shared, best-effort'; 'High-volume or sustained data transfers may be subject to bandwidth limits, rate limiting, and fair-use policies'

reliability_note: The cloud Reverse Proxy is beta, is shared and best-effort, and carries a named but unnumbered bandwidth and rate-limit clause; L4 services support TCP and UDP, and HTTP services do not.

evidence.proved: 'UDP | L4 | UDP relay with session tracking. The proxy accepts UDP packets on the service's listen port and forwards them to your backend.'

'Cloud-hosted usage limits: NetBird's cloud-hosted Reverse Proxy is provided on a shared, best-effort basis. High-volume or sustained data transfers may be subject to bandwidth limits, rate limiting, and fair-use policies'

notes: 2026-10-23: the cloud plan has a public ingress with UDP. NetBird Reverse Proxy offers L4 'TCP', 'UDP' and 'TLS' service modes, and a UDP service is 'a UDP relay with session tracking. The proxy accepts UDP packets on the service's listen port and forwards them to your backend. Sessions are reaped after an idle timeout'. Cloud domains are free and appear 'with a Free badge'. The meter is discretionary: 'NetBird's cloud-hosted Reverse Proxy is provided on a shared, best-effort basis. High-volume or sustained data transfers may be subject to bandwidth limits, rate limiting, and fair-use policies', and 'These restrictions do not apply if you self-host NetBird'. Whether the Free plan is entitled to the feature is not stated on either the pricing page or the docs page.

extras.transit_note: peers negotiate a direct WireGuard path; the operator's relay carries bytes only when that fails, at an unpublished rate

limits_note: counts of things, not rates, so no vocabulary kind names them: 100 machines plus 10 per user
binding_note: No byte figure exists for the cloud Reverse Proxy, so 1 TiB/month is planned against a sentence rather than a number. The L4 mode accepts TCP and UDP, so the transport test passes, and the reverse proxy is free to use; what fails first is the unwritten fair-use clause, with self-hosting named by the vendor as the way the restrictions do not apply.
